clue.text: Musical work brought out by Police?

definitions.text: Musical work brought out by Police?

parts.words: Musical work brought out by Police?
parts.note: read musically it is a volume of written notes, a score; read literally it is what an officer pulls from a pocket to take down a statement

explanation.surface: A band called the Police releases a new album.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P suggests the rock band, but the question mark invites the plain picture of a constable producing a pocket book to record details.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers carry a small pad for jotting evidence, and a book of musical notation could be called the same.

clue.text: Swelling small number expected, including an extra fifty

parts.note: NO is the standard abbreviation for number

indicators.note: the word for expected takes the extra letter inside it

parts.note: something expected is due
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, here added as an extra

explanation.surface: A doctor counts a few swellings and is expecting one more.
explanation.definitionFit: A nodule is a small rounded lump or growth in body tissue.

clue.text: Fat old women highly unlikely to be leading

indicators.note: the word meaning highly unlikely goes in front of the abbreviations for old women

parts.note: a tall story is one that is hard to believe

explanation.surface: Overweight elderly ladies are improbable front-runners in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is rendered animal fat, once used for candles and soap.

clue.text: Argue motorcyclist's gone round first part of course

indicators.note: the rider's word wraps around the opening letter as if circling it

parts.note: a biker rides a motorcycle; the 's stands for has

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A rider rows with officials after lapping the start of the track.
explanation.definitionFit: To bicker is to squabble over petty matters.

clue.text: Working to get back into a healthier condition?

definitions.text: Working to get back into a healthier condition?

parts.words: Working to get back into a healthier condition?
parts.note: the phrase sounds like a general recovery effort, but read as working on a person's back and bones it names a manipulative therapy

explanation.surface: Someone toils to regain fitness after illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get back into' looks like 'return to', but 'back' is the body part this treatment manipulates.
explanation.definitionFit: This therapy treats bodily disorders by manipulating the spine, muscles and joints.

clue.text: His activities attracted a good deal of interest

definitions.text: His activities attracted a good deal of interest

parts.words: His activities attracted a good deal of interest
parts.note: interest seems to mean public attention, but it is the money charged on a loan, which this lender sets excessively high

explanation.surface: A man's doings drew a lot of public attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender who charges exorbitant rates earns large sums in charges on loans.

clue.text: Unusually short slinky top — it's fastened in a special way

definitions.text: it's fastened in a special way

indicators.note: the letters are set out in an unusual new order
the word slinky is cut short by losing its final letter

explanation.surface: An oddly brief clingy top is done up in a distinctive manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims slinky to SLINK; 'Unusually' then rearranges SLINK with TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of knot is tied so that it can be undone by pulling one end.

clue.text: Fungus mostly growing wild in Madagascar

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go inside the country code

parts.note: RM is the international vehicle code for Madagascar

indicators.note: the letters run wild into a new order
most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A fungus spreads unchecked across the island of Madagascar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' gives GROWIN; 'wild' rearranges it to INGWO, which goes in RM.
explanation.definitionFit: This skin infection is caused by a fungus, not a worm, despite its name.

clue.text: Receipt given by nuns for musical instrument

parts.note: REC is an abbreviation for receipt
a body of nuns forms a religious order

explanation.surface: Sisters hand over a receipt when they sell a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A recorder is a woodwind instrument played by blowing into a mouthpiece.

clue.text: Priest, Catholic brought in to fill appointment that's sensitive

indicators.note: the priest and abbreviation are placed inside the word for an appointment

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting
Eli is the priest in the biblical book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A Catholic cleric is drafted in to take up a post that is touchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delicate needs careful handling, like a tricky or touchy issue.

clue.text: External courses

parts.note: it suggests extramural study, but means courses of a meal eaten outdoors

explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor meal served in the open air may run to several dishes.

clue.text: Lone rook flies round observer

indicators.note: the letters fly about and land in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A solitary black bird circles a watcher.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker who watches without taking part is a spectator.

clue.text: Series about gardens makes you spit

indicators.note: the abbreviation for series goes around the gardens

parts.note: Kew Gardens are the Royal Botanic Gardens in west London

explanation.surface: A run of programmes on horticulture leaves you spluttering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spit' looks like the verb, but it is the noun: a rod for roasting meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is a long pin pushed through meat, like a roasting rod.

clue.text: Where you may find corpse in centre of plot?

definitions.text: Where you may find corpse in centre of plot?

parts.words: Where you may find corpse in centre of plot?
parts.note: a corpse at the centre of a plot suggests a murder mystery, but a burial plot lies in a great ancient cemetery

explanation.surface: A detective novel's body turns up at the heart of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means a large ancient cemetery, literally a city of the dead.

clue.text: Favourite track

parts.note: it suggests a best-loved song, but the favourite is the horse tipped to win, running on the ground where horses compete

explanation.definitionFit: Horses, including the bookmakers' favourite, compete on a turf circuit.

clue.text: Sacrifice made by electricity regulators in Greek capital

parts.note: OFFER was the UK Office of Electricity Regulation

indicators.note: the capital, or opening letter, of the word Greek is taken

explanation.surface: Power-industry watchdogs perform an offering in Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek capital' suggests Athens, but it is only the capital letter of 'Greek'. OFFER was the 1990s British electricity watchdog.
explanation.definitionFit: An offering is something given up to a god, like a sacrifice.

clue.text: Carefree bird, one flying across Austria

indicators.note: the scrambled letters span across the abbreviation for Austria
the letters fly into a new order

parts.note: A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: A happy bird is one that migrates over the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' looks like the definition's partner, but it is anagram fodder; 'flying' makes DEBONIR, which 'across' spreads around Austria's A.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave and confident, with a light-hearted, easy-going manner.

clue.text: Timetable suggested by a couple of educationists in German school

indicators.note: the two letters sit inside the German word

parts.note: Schule is the German word for school

indicators.note: the first two letters of the next word are taken

explanation.surface: Two teachers in a German school draw up the timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a plan of times when events happen, like a programme.

clue.text: Parisian's cape blown in the wind?

parts.note: a Parisian is French
Cape Horn is the southern tip of South America

explanation.surface: A Parisian's cloak flaps in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wind' suggests the weather, but means the wind section of an orchestra, where this brass instrument is played.
explanation.definitionFit: This brass instrument is played by blowing and sits in the wind section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Item carved in Black Forest (allegedly)

parts.note: it suggests wood carving in the German forest region, but Black Forest names a chocolate and cherry cake that is sliced

explanation.surface: A woodcarver's souvenir from the Black Forest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Forest is a German region famous for wood carving; '(allegedly)' notes that this cake may not come from there at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich layered cake is cut into slices, as with the chocolate and cherry Black Forest variety.

clue.text: Foreign currency English group needed in Panama

indicators.note: the abbreviation and group go inside the code for Panama

parts.note: PA is the international code for Panama
a set is a group

explanation.surface: An English party needs local money in Panama.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the money of Spain before the euro.

clue.text: Butt of jokes gets upset about a pair of spectacles

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the pair of round shapes
the letters are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of round lenses

explanation.surface: A comedian's target gets cross over a pair of glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt' could mislead toward the backside; 'upset' scrambles the letters to STGE, which 'about' wraps around the two round lenses.
explanation.definitionFit: A stooge is a comic's foil, the one made to look foolish.

clue.text: Ran together

parts.note: it suggests jogging side by side, but means a couple who fled together to marry in secret

explanation.definitionFit: A couple who run off secretly to marry do so as one.

clue.text: A form of paper stuck on books that's clear?

indicators.note: the books abbreviation is attached to the end
a different form of the word means its letters rearranged

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A sort of paper is pasted onto volumes to make them see-through.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obvious is plain to see, as in an evident truth.

clue.text: Waxwing plummeting from a great height?

definitions.text: Waxwing plummeting from a great height?

parts.words: Waxwing plummeting from a great height?
parts.note: a waxwing is a bird, but here it means a wing made of wax, worn by the Greek youth who flew too near the sun

explanation.surface: A songbird drops out of the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the wax holding his feathered wings melted when he flew too close to the sun, and he fell into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical son of Daedalus flew on wings of wax and feathers and fell to his death.

clue.text: Byzantine legate or his trusted friend?

indicators.note: byzantine means intricate and tortuous, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A scheming papal envoy or his confidant.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means a second self, a close confidant.

clue.text: What may hold order

definitions.meaning: a band worn on the leg to hold up a stocking
the Most Noble Order of the ... is England's senior order of chivalry

explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a command, but it is a knightly order.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg band keeps stockings up, and the oldest English order of knighthood is named for one.

clue.text: Big copper formerly seen to give and receive smackers?

parts.note: OS is short for outsize
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
late means former, as in the late president

explanation.surface: An outsize policeman was once seen to trade blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big copper' suggests a burly policeman, and 'smackers' blows, but smackers are kisses.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiss is to plant smackers on someone, the formal Latin-derived term.
